title: Bathtub wastewater overflow trip lever repair
subtitle: San Francisco · concealed waste-and-overflow repair
intro: The trip lever is seized inside the concealed waste-and-overflow plumbing behind the bathroom wall. Removing it from above has not worked; the reported fallback is access from below, through the ceiling of the storage unit, which means opening and later patching drywall. This dashboard organises the three quotes received on 2026-08-30, eleven San Francisco contractor candidates checked against the State licence database, independent cost benchmarks, the hiring plan, and every item that still needs a human decision.

problem_facts.detail: Bathtub wastewater overflow trip lever, stuck inside the concealed waste-and-overflow plumbing behind the wall.
The overflow is in a hard-to-reach area. More than five licensed plumbers reportedly would not remove it from above for fear of damaging the hidden plumbing.
Work from below, through the storage unit underneath. May require opening the drywall ceiling to reach the plumbing.
Remove the overflow from above if it can be done without damaging the concealed assembly.
One provider for drywall and plumbing on a single job, experienced with delicate work in a tenant-occupied unit.
